interpretations.rationale: Receipt 78d56323ae6646da8140c38ebed9bd1c (exit 0, ten events, no parse loss) resolves both comparisons of the corrected declaration. Comparison 0 is violated by witness event index 9: with RestoreCommittedLogs on, no snapshot and 8402 committed entries (commit index 8402, admission event index 8), NewRaft had not returned after the bounded 15 second wait. Comparison 1 holds at evaluated event index 7: the same restart with 8002 committed entries returned in 2 ms, so the two sizes bracket the failure and rule out general replay slowness. Source mechanism: NewRaft creates fsmMutateCh with capacity 128 (api.go:558-561) and starts the FSM, main and snapshot goroutines only after the startup work at api.go:632-639, while restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) calls processLogs, which pushes one message per MaxAppendEntries batch into that queue (raft.go:1296-1320); a replay needing more than 128 batches blocks on an unconsumed channel inside NewRaft with no retry, timeout or fallback in that path. Consequence: the node never finishes starting, so duties that depend on it (elections, replication, convergence) are stalled indefinitely rather than bounded; the boundary near 8192 committed entries with default MaxAppendEntries of 64 and default TrailingLogs of 10240 keeps this inside ordinary settings. The earlier receipt 04fccedbacf54df3b7064fd16fa57b26 already witnessed the violation but could not complete the control because both sizes shared one result event name; it is retained as prior evidence of the same behaviour.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading establishes the mechanism: NewRaft initialises configurations to its zero value, restoreSnapshot is the only producer that can supply a configuration from persistent state (api.go:655-681), and the only other producer is the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) starting at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs before that scan and calls setCommitIndex(commitIndex) then processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs forwards LogConfiguration entries to the FSM (raft.go:1366-1391) and never updates r.configurations. With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, every committed configuration entry at or below the restored commit index is therefore invisible to the node after restart. A native construction probe of a bootstrapped single node (CommitTrackingLogs, no snapshot, 10 applied entries) reproduced the predicted difference: with the flag on the event was {after_latest_index:0, after_servers:0, after_has_vote:false, after_commit_index:11, after_last_applied:11, before_latest_index:1, snapshots:0} and the library logged 'initial configuration: index=0 servers=[]'; with the flag off the same restart reported {after_latest_index:1, after_servers:1, after_has_vote:true}. scope.description: Boot a single-voter cluster with CommitTrackingLogs, commit ten entries, shut down, restart from the same stores, then sample the node's raft state every 10 ms for a bounded 1500 ms window (ElectionTimeout is 50 ms) and report whether leadership was ever acquired. Run with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs true and false.
assumptions: A single-voter configuration normally regains leadership within a few election timeouts, which the 1500 ms window covers by a wide margin.
No snapshot exists, so the snapshot path cannot supply the configuration.
Sampling does not perturb the node; the state is read through the library's own accessor.
excluded: Whole-package or repository test suites.
Multi-voter election outcomes, which the single-voter scenario cannot witness.
The startup-blocking finding, which is a separate question.

basis.prefix: The harness boots one node with CommitTrackingLogs and RestoreCommittedLogs, applies ten commands, records the committed configuration index, shuts down, and restarts with NewRaft on the same logs, stable and snapshots stores plus a fresh inmem transport. It then polls getState() for a bounded window and emits authority_after_restart with became_leader, the final state name, the sample window and the configuration index observed after the restart; a startup_before_restart event carries the same mode identity and the pre-restart state, and no production logic is modified.
basis.responsibility: The library owns the state a node resumes with: once a committed configuration exists in its log, a restart must not leave it permanently unable to participate, which the caller cannot repair through the public API.

comparisons.description: A single-voter cluster restarted from its own committed state is expected to regain leadership inside the bounded window; the defect prediction is that it never campaigns.
Control: the identical restart without the flag is expected to reach Leader, separating the lost configuration from any general restart delay.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading establishes the mechanism: NewRaft initialises configurations to its zero value, restoreSnapshot is the only producer that can supply a configuration from persistent state (api.go:655-681), and the only other producer is the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) starting at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs before that scan and calls setCommitIndex(commitIndex) then processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs forwards LogConfiguration entries to the FSM (raft.go:1366-1391) and never updates r.configurations. With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, every committed configuration entry at or below the restored commit index is therefore invisible to the node after restart. A native construction probe of a bootstrapped single node (CommitTrackingLogs, no snapshot, 10 applied entries) reproduced the predicted difference: with the flag on the event was {after_latest_index:0, after_servers:0, after_has_vote:false, after_commit_index:11, after_last_applied:11, before_latest_index:1, snapshots:0} and the library logged 'initial configuration: index=0 servers=[]'; with the flag off the same restart reported {after_latest_index:1, after_servers:1, after_has_vote:true}. The probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the formal comparison is left to the submitted experiment. Consequence under the stated conditions: the restarted node's own membership view is the pre-restart snapshot value or empty, so runFollower's 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) prevent it from campaigning, and quorumSize() is computed over a configuration that contradicts the committed log (raft.go:1087-1094). Counterevidence examined: a snapshot can legitimately supply the configuration (api.go:677-678) but only as of snapshot.ConfigurationIndex, which cannot cover a configuration committed after that snapshot; appendEntries processes only entries it newly appends (raft.go:1594-1621); leaderLoop only promotes latest to committed (raft.go:797-799). Limitations: the finding is scoped to the stated configuration and store conditions; the snapshot-present variant remains a registered gap; only a controller receipt can make this a completed comparison.

The admission events (0 and 2) confirm both cases started from before_latest_index 1 with one server, so the only difference is whether restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied. Its events 0-3 repeat the no-snapshot pair with the same values as receipt 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175: mode on yields after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0 and after_has_vote false while after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11 were restored, and the mode off control yields index 1 with one voter. interpretations.rationale: Source: NewRaft's FSM queue is created with capacity 128 (api.go:558-561) and the FSM, main and snapshot goroutines are only started after the startup work at api.go:632-639; restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) calls processLogs, which pushes one message per batch of MaxAppendEntries entries into that queue (raft.go:1296-1320). A committed backlog needing more than 128 batches therefore has no consumer while NewRaft runs. A native construction probe with the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 measured a sharp boundary: 8002 committed entries (126 batches) returned from NewRaft in 3 ms, while 8402 entries (132 batches) had not returned after a bounded 15 second wait. That probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the submitted experiment repeats both sizes under controller execution and only its receipt can make this a completed comparison.
counterevidence: A backlog that stays at or below the queue capacity returns promptly, so the failure is not general slowness of log replay.
limitations: No receipt yet; the account rests on source reading plus a native probe.
The interval is a bounded wait, not an infinite-run proof; a later repair or a substantially different schedule is not excluded.
The queue capacity is taken from the source constant, not measured.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 04fccedbacf54df3b7064fd16fa57b26 (exit 0, ten events, no parse loss) witnesses the prediction: with RestoreCommittedLogs on, no snapshot, 8402 committed entries and a restored commit index of 8402 (event index 8), the restart reported newraft_returned false after a bounded 15 second wait (event index 9), so comparison 0 is violated with witness event index 9. The paired below-capacity case is retained as an observation, not as a completed comparison: event index 7 reports newraft_returned true after 0 ms for 8002 entries, but comparison 1 returned unknown because both backlog cases shared one result event name, so each comparison looked for the other case's admission and the controller marked the other result incomplete; the corrected declaration gives each size its own result event and is submitted as a successor experiment. Source mechanism: NewRaft creates fsmMutateCh with capacity 128 (api.go:558-561) and starts the FSM, main and snapshot goroutines only after the startup work at api.go:632-639, while restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) calls processLogs, which pushes one message per batch of MaxAppendEntries entries into that queue (raft.go:1296-1320). A replay needing more than 128 batches therefore blocks on an unconsumed channel inside NewRaft, with no retry, timeout or fallback in that path. Consequence under the stated conditions: the node never finishes starting, so a node that should resume service after a restart does not, and every duty depending on it (elections, replication, convergence) is stalled indefinitely rather than bounded; with the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 the boundary sits near 8192 committed entries and the default TrailingLogs of 10240 allows a log that large before any snapshot.
counterevidence: The sub-capacity case returned immediately (0 ms for 8002 entries), so the outcome is not general slowness of replaying committed logs.
No snapshot existed in either case, so the blocking is independent of snapshot restore.
limitations: The failing case is a bounded 15 second wait, not an infinite-run proof; a different schedule or a later repair is not excluded by this observation alone.
The queue capacity of 128 and the batch size are taken from the source, not measured.
The configuration-loss finding under the parent question is a separate defect and is not part of this account.
